title: Accuracy Versus Base Rate Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Prediction Accuracy
Base Rate
Baseline Forecast
Predictive Fidelity
description: A Chart.js lab comparing a synthetic model's accuracy with the always-predict-the-majority baseline on seeded cohorts of 200 learners, with sliders for the base rate and the model's signal strength and a warning when the accuracy carries no evidence.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

learningObjectives: Judge whether a reported accuracy demonstrates predictive value by comparing it with the always-predict-the-majority baseline as the base rate changes.

accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: Okabe-Ito blue and orange, with legend and value labels

simulation.modelType: Seeded synthetic cohort with a calibrated binormal forecaster
equations: y ~ Bernoulli(b); x = z + delta/2 if y = 1, z - delta/2 if y = 0, z ~ Normal(0, 1)
forecast f = 1 / (1 + exp(-(logit(b) + delta x))); call 'correct' when f >= 0.5
baseline accuracy = max(share correct, share incorrect)
assumptions: The separation 0.924 matches the chapter's synthetic BKT model in expectation (AUC about 0.743, accuracy about 0.705 at base rate 0.635).
The first cohort uses seed 177, whose draw reproduces the chapter's counts (127 and 141 of 200).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge claims against a baseline, then probe with parameter changes
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a paired comparison chart
keyQuestions: What would a model that knows nothing score on this cohort?
How large must the lift be before it counts as evidence?
Why can an informative model tie the baseline when success is very common?
commonMisconceptions: A high accuracy means the model is informative.
Accuracy can be compared across cohorts with different base rates.
A model with no lift in accuracy must have no signal.
assessmentOpportunities: State the baseline and lift for a reported accuracy and judge it.
Rewrite an accuracy claim so it reports the baseline in the same sentence.
